⚠️ WARNING: Colosseum Ticket Name Trap ⚠️

DO NOT put the same name on multiple tickets!

The official booking system lets you buy 2+ tickets under ONE name with zero warning. But at the entrance, security checks the ID of EVERY visitor.

If the name on the ticket doesn't match the person's ID, they will DENY ENTRY. No refund, no exceptions. You lose your money.

TIP: Each ticket MUST have the full name of the actual person entering. Double-check all tickets before paying. The system won't warn you about this issue.

観客席に立つと、昔ここで熱狂的な観戦があったというのが想像できて、普通にタイムスリップした気分になります。こんな感じで“歴史の中に自分がいる”感覚がかなり強かったです。

地下エリアも見学できて、当時の舞台裏や動物・人の移動ルートなどが残っていて、想像以上にリアルに歴史を感じました。表から見るだけとは全然違います。

title: Colosseum

text:
Colosseum Essentials: How to See Rome’s Icon in a Hurry

The Colosseum is Rome’s most iconic ancient landmark, built between 70–80 AD and preserved today as a UNESCO World Heritage site. During the Roman Empire, this massive arena hosted gladiator battles, animal hunts, and even staged naval battles.
Getting there is simple using the Metro. If you are staying near Termini, take Line B just two stops to the "Colosseo" station. If you are near the Vatican, take Line A to Termini and transfer to Line B.
For the best photos, head to the Palatine Hill overlooking the Roman Forum for a sweeping view of the structure. To go inside and explore its amazing history, be sure to purchase your tickets well in advance, as they sell out quickly.

name: Ross Daniels
text: I had many thoughts on entering the Colosseum. Yes, it is a must visit. However I wondered that if the stones could talk they would almost certainly scream because alongside the monumental structure exemplifying the brilliance of the Roman Empire is the brutality and extraordinary cruelty that went on. I understand it was originally built to manage upwards of 80,000 people with amazing architecture allowing crowds to disburse easily. Originally everything about it, including the retractable roof and a sort of elevator system that launched animals and gladiators, is a tribute to ancient engineering. However it is impossible to allow the brilliance of architecture to overwhelm the fact that thousands of animals and humans perished simply for entertainment. And the further I dug into the nature of the entertainment the more I was repulsed. However one cannot visit Rome without going to this place.

title: Colosseum
name: Selma Avdic
text:
Koloseum u Rimu jedan je od najpoznatijih spomenika iz doba Rimskog carstva i simbol njegove moći i veličine. Izgrađen je u prvom vijeku nove ere, za vrijeme cara Vespazijana, a dovršen za vladavine njegovog sina Titusa. Njegovo otvaranje obilježeno je velikim igrama koje su trajale više dana i okupile ogroman broj gledalaca.
Ova monumentalna građevina ima eliptičan oblik i impresivne dimenzije. Dugačak je oko 189 metara, širok 156 metara, a visok približno 48 metara. Procjenjuje se da je mogao primiti između 50.000 i 65.000 ljudi, što ga čini jednim od najvećih amfiteatara ikada izgrađenih. Građen je od kamena, betona i cigle, a njegova konstrukcija pokazuje izuzetno razvijene inženjerske sposobnosti starih Rimljana.
Unutrašnjost Koloseuma bila je pažljivo organizovana. Centralni dio činila je arena, prekrivena pijeskom, gdje su se odvijale borbe. Ispod arene nalazio se hipogeum – mreža podzemnih hodnika i prostorija u kojima su se nalazili gladijatori i divlje životinje prije izlaska pred publiku. Posebni mehanizmi omogućavali su brzo podizanje životinja i scenografije na površinu, što je dodatno doprinosilo spektaklu.
U Koloseumu su se održavale razne priredbe, među kojima su najpoznatije gladijatorske borbe, lov na divlje životinje i javna pogubljenja. Ove igre bile su važan dio rimskog društva i služile su za zabavu, ali i za demonstraciju moći države.
Tokom historije, Koloseum je pretrpio brojna oštećenja. Nakon pada Rimskog carstva izgubio je svoju prvobitnu funkciju i korišten je kao tvrđava, skladište, pa čak i kao izvor građevinskog materijala. Zemljotresi su također doprinijeli njegovom djelimičnom rušenju. Ipak, veliki dio građevine je sačuvan i danas.
Danas je Koloseum jedan od najvažnijih kulturno i historijskih spomenika u Italiji i nezaobilazna turistička atrakcija. Njegova veličina, arhitektura i bogata historija svjedoče o snazi i naprednosti antičkog Rima. Kao takav, Koloseum ostaje trajni simbol prošlosti koji i danas izaziva divljenje ljudi širom svijeta.Toliko ljepote na jednom mjestu neopisivo.
Selma Avdić 🥰

text:
Koloseum w Rzymie to absolutny klasyk – wygląda tak epicko, że aż człowiek spodziewa się, że za rogiem wyskoczy gladiator z mieczem i zapyta, czy masz bilet 😄🏛️

Ale kiedy już wejdziesz do środka… zaczyna się prawdziwa arena walki. Tylko zamiast lwów i wojowników masz tłumy turystów i system zwiedzania, który najwyraźniej projektował ktoś po krótkiej drzemce. Kierunek zwiedzania? Bardziej sugestia niż zasada. Idziesz, skręcasz, zawracasz i nagle nie wiesz, czy oglądasz nowe miejsce, czy już trzeci raz to samo 😅

Organizacja ma swój unikalny klimat – coś pomiędzy “jakoś to będzie” a “odkryj to sam, śmiałku”. Trochę jak escape room, tylko nikt nie tłumaczy zasad.

A bilety? No cóż… my wybraliśmy tryb hardcore i wbiliśmy się w kolejkę jak na promocję w supermarkecie. Było napięcie, była strategia, było lekkie przepychanie – czyli pełen pakiet emocji. Ale udało się. Czuliśmy się jak zwycięzcy igrzysk 🏆

Podsumowanie: Koloseum zachwyca, ale logistycznie to mały survival. Warto – tylko zabierzcie cierpliwość i może kompas 😉

Đấu trường La Mã hay Đại hý trường La Mã được biết đến đầu tiên dưới cái tên Amphitheatrum Flavium theo tiếng Latinh hoặc Anfitea tro Flavio tiếng Ý, sau này gọi là Colosseum hay Colosseo, là một đấu trường lớn ở thành phố Roma. Công suất chứa lúc mới xây xong là 50.000 khán giả. Đấu trường được sử dụng cho các võ sĩ giác đấu và nô lệ có nguồn gốc tù binh chiến tranh thi đấu và trình diễn công chúng. Đấu trường được xây dựng khoảng năm 70–80 dưới thời hoàng đế Vespasian. Đây là công trình lớn nhất được xây ở Đế chế La Mã được hoàn thành năm 80 dưới thời Titus, với nhiều chỉnh sửa dưới thời hoàng đế Domitian.

Đấu trường Colosseum vẫn được sử dụng gần 500 năm với những bằng chứng ghi chép được về trận đấu thế kỷ 6 – rất lâu sau khi Đế chế La Mã sụp đổ năm 476. Ngoài sử dụng làm nơi đấu của võ sỹ, nơi đây còn được dùng làm biểu diễn công chúng, tập trận giả trên biển, săn thú, kịch cổ điển. Công trình này dần dần không được sử dụng làm nơi giải trí nữa thời Trung Cổ. Sau này, đấu trường được sử dụng làm nhà ở, cửa hàng, nhà thờ, pháp trường...

Dù hiện nay bị hoang phế nhiều do động đất và nạn cướp đá, Colosseum vẫn từ lâu được xem là biểu tượng của Đế chế La Mã và là một trong những mẫu kiến trúc La Mã đẹp nhất còn sót lại. Đây là điểm tham quan hấp dẫn của Roma và vẫn còn nhiều liên hệ với Giáo hội Công giáo. Hằng năm vào Thứ sáu Tuần Thánh, giáo hoàng vẫn chủ sự nghi lễ Đàng Thánh Giá tại Colosseo.

L’edificio ospitava combattimenti fra gladiatori e spettacoli come lotte fra animali pericolosi ed esotici, cacce e naucomachie. title: Colosseum
name: Gianluca M.
text:
Il Colosseo, chiamato in origine Anfiteatro Flavio, è il monumento simbolo di Roma e uno dei più celebri del mondo antico. Si trova tra il Palatino, il Foro Romano e il Celio ed è il più grande anfiteatro mai costruito nell’Impero romano.

Costruzione

Fu iniziato dall’imperatore Vespasiano intorno al 70-72 d.C. e inaugurato dal figlio Tito nell’80 d.C.; alcuni lavori furono completati poi sotto Domiziano.

Venne costruito dove prima si trovava il lago artificiale della Domus Aurea di Nerone: una scelta anche politica, per restituire al popolo uno spazio che prima apparteneva al lusso imperiale.

Il nome “Colosseo” deriva probabilmente dal vicino Colosso di Nerone, enorme statua bronzea collocata nella zona.

Architettura

Il Colosseo è un capolavoro di ingegneria romana:

forma ellittica;
circa 189 metri di lunghezza e 156 metri di larghezza;
altezza di quasi 50 metri;
capacità stimata tra 50.000 e 80.000 spettatori.

Era organizzato in modo rigidamente gerarchico:

posti migliori per senatori e autorità;
livelli superiori per cittadini comuni e donne.
Gli ingressi numerati permettevano di svuotare rapidamente l’edificio: un sistema molto moderno, quasi uno stadio contemporaneo ante litteram.

A cosa serviva

Nel Colosseo si svolgevano:

combattimenti tra gladiatori;
cacce ad animali esotici (venationes);
esecuzioni pubbliche;
spettacoli e rievocazioni.

Contrariamente a una credenza popolare, le grandi battaglie navali (naumachiae) nel Colosseo sono ancora discusse dagli storici e non furono una pratica abituale.

L’ipogeo

Sotto l’arena si trova il complesso sistema di corridoi chiamato ipogeo:

gabbie per animali;
montacarichi;
macchinari scenici;
passaggi per gladiatori e personale.

Era una vera “macchina teatrale” dell’antichità.

Declino

Dopo la fine dell’Impero romano d’Occidente e il progressivo declino dei giochi, il Colosseo cambiò funzione:

fortezza medievale;
abitazioni e botteghe;
cava di materiali (molti marmi furono riutilizzati per altri edifici romani).
Terremoti, spoliazioni e tempo ne compromisero parte della struttura.

Colosseo e cristianesimo

Dal XVIII secolo il Colosseo fu consacrato come luogo legato alla memoria dei martiri cristiani, anche se il rapporto diretto tra Colosseo e martirio di massa dei cristiani è più complesso e meno documentato di quanto spesso si pensi.

Oggi ospita la tradizionale Via Crucis del Papa il Venerdì Santo.

Curiosità
È stato inserito tra le Nuove Sette Meraviglie del Mondo nel 2007.
È il monumento più visitato d’Italia.

Questo monumento non ha bisogno di recensioni, lo conoscono tutti per la sua bellezza. Vorrei invece dare delle indicazioni per le prenotazioni e le visite, visto che non è proprio facile districarsi tra i vari pacchetti che si trovano in rete.
Cominciamo col dire che l’acquisto del biglietto sul sito ufficiale costa molto meno che su altre piattaforme. Il biglietto combinato con i fori imperiali costa 18 euro a persona e i bambini sono gratuiti. Il problema è riuscire a farlo….. I biglietti escono on-line esattamente 30 giorni prima del giorno che vogliamo visitarlo ed esattamente all’ora della visita. Ad esempio se vogliamo prenotare il biglietto l’1 giugno alle 14, le vendite usciranno alle 14 del 1 maggio. Ci sono nuove fasce orarie che escono ogni 15 minuti. Ci ho messo ben 2 ore per acquistare i biglietti, anche perchè il sito si sovraccarica e non consente di terminare la prenotazione. E i biglietti terminano in pochi minuti. Quindi bisogna armarsi di pazienza.

Una volta sul posto l’ingresso si trova di fronte all’arco di Costantino.

Ci sono poi altri biglietti che consentono di visitare anche i sotterranei del Colosseo. Ma credo che la vista migliore sia quella dalle gradinate come abbiamo fatto noi.

An Unforgettable Walk Through History: The Colosseum
​If there is one landmark that lives up to every ounce of its global hype, it is the Colosseum. Standing in the heart of Rome, this massive travertine amphitheater isn’t just a pile of ancient stones; it is a visceral, awe-inspiring bridge to a world 2,000 years in the past.
​Why It’s a Must-Visit
​The Scale is Staggering: No photograph can truly capture the sheer magnitude of the structure. Walking through the same stone corridors as ancient Roman spectators, you feel the weight of history in a way that is both humbling and electrifying.

I visited the Colosseum at night, so I didn’t have the chance to go inside—but even from the outside, it was absolutely breathtaking.

Beautifully illuminated after dark, the Colosseum stands as a powerful reminder of ancient Rome. Built nearly 2,000 years ago, it was once used for gladiator contests and large public spectacles, and seeing it in person really gives you a sense of its scale and history.

The atmosphere around the area is lively, with streetlights, small vendors, and street sellers walking around with glowing items. It does get quite crowded, especially in the evening, which makes it a bit challenging to take clean photos without people in the frame.

That said, the energy of the place adds to the experience in its own way.

Even without going inside, it was still a memorable visit. I’d love to come back during the day next time to explore more.

title: Colosseum
name: Jonathan Popp
text:
Das Kolosseum in Rom ist eines der beeindruckendsten Bauwerke der Antike und definitiv ein Highlight für jeden, der sich für Geschichte, Architektur oder einfach für besondere Orte interessiert.

Schon beim ersten Anblick wirkt das Kolosseum überwältigend: Die schiere Größe und die gut erhaltene Struktur machen sofort klar, welche Bedeutung dieses Amphitheater im Römischen Reich hatte. Es wurde im 1. Jahrhundert n. Chr. erbaut und bot Platz für etwa 50.000 Zuschauer – eine enorme Leistung für diese Zeit.

Beim Rundgang durch das Innere bekommt man einen guten Eindruck davon, wie die Gladiatorenkämpfe und andere Veranstaltungen abliefen. Besonders spannend ist der Blick in den unterirdischen Bereich (Hypogäum), wo früher Tiere und Kämpfer auf ihren Einsatz warteten. Die Kombination aus Geschichte und Vorstellungskraft macht den Besuch sehr lebendig.

Ein weiterer Pluspunkt ist die Lage: Mitten im Herzen von Rom, in unmittelbarer Nähe zu anderen Sehenswürdigkeiten wie dem Forum Romanum, lässt sich der Besuch gut in einen größeren Sightseeing-Tag integrieren.

Allerdings gibt es auch ein paar Nachteile. Das Kolosseum ist oft sehr stark besucht, was zu langen Wartezeiten und vielen Menschenmengen führen kann. Es lohnt sich daher, Tickets im Voraus zu buchen oder früh am Morgen zu kommen. Außerdem sind einige Bereiche stark restauriert oder abgesperrt, was den authentischen Eindruck teilweise etwas einschränkt.

Insgesamt ist das Kolosseum aber ein absolutes Muss. Die historische Bedeutung, die beeindruckende Architektur und die besondere Atmosphäre machen den Besuch zu einem unvergesslichen Erlebnis. Wer in Rom ist und das Kolosseum auslässt, verpasst eines der wichtigsten Wahrzeichen der Welt.

title: Colosseum
name: Cristian
text:
The Colosseum remains the beating heart of Rome, a colossal testament to human ingenuity and the dark complexities of our nature. I have had the privilege of visiting it across all seasons, and its majesty never fades. Whether I am exploring its labyrinthine interior or simply standing in its shadow to admire its imposing exterior during a quick Roman getaway, it never fails to command respect.
It is truly staggering to consider what was built in those ancient times. The Flavian Amphitheatre serves as the architectural blueprint for modern stadiums, yet its history is far more visceral. It was a stage for blood and sand, fueled by the infamous Roman philosophy of "Panem et Circenses" (Bread and Circuses). The emperors knew that as long as the masses were fed and entertained, their power remained unchallenged.
Today, it stands as a silent museum, but its lessons are timeless. While the gladiators are gone, the human psyche remains remarkably unchanged. Even now, if you provide "bread and circuses," you can influence the masses at will. It is a cynical reflection, perhaps, but standing before those arches, you realize that while the stones have weathered, our fundamental instincts have not. It is an architectural marvel and a somber mirror to humanity.

text:
Colosseum looks grand and easily accessible via MRT/metro station and bus stop right outside it.

Colosseum with access to Arena along with Roman Forum, Palatine Hille & other SUPER sites are sold only a week in advance, but others like Colosseum with underground & attic or guided tours are sold from several weeks in advance & they always appear to be sold out for any dates that you check. I personally feel that you won’t be missing much if you don’t visit the attic/underground. The arena and the walk around the colosseum gives you a pretty good view of the entire amphitheatre.

There is a timed entry only for Colosseum, but for Roman Forum & Palatine Hill you can visit it any time of the day of the ticket. You can reach Colosseum some 15 minutes prior to your entry time and easily go in without long queues.

I recommend booking the tickets only through the official website (https://ticketing.colosseo.it/en/) and not through any 3rd party websites. Children below 18 years get a free entry to Colosseum when booked through the official website, but in other websites, they are also charged a full price. Adult entry ticket price is also lesser in official website.

Time in the underground is limited to 30 minutes making this part of a tour rushed where there is now enough space to accommodate more time.

If you're on a standard tour or entry ticket the main 2 levels have more than enough to keep you occupied and educated with informative displays and plenty of text to read. Most tours skip a lot of the displays because you would end up spending all day in here and many tours are limited to between 1 and 3 hours including the Roman Forum.

title: Colosseum
name: Dibakar Bhakta
text:
The Colosseum stands as one of the most iconic and awe-inspiring landmarks of the ancient world, a monumental reminder of the grandeur of the Roman Empire. Located in the heart of Rome, this विशाल amphitheatre continues to captivate millions of visitors with its scale, history, and architectural brilliance.

Built between 70–80 AD under emperors Vespasian and Titus, the Colosseum once hosted gladiatorial contests, animal hunts, and public spectacles that drew crowds of up to 50,000 spectators. Even in its partially ruined state, the structure’s engineering sophistication is remarkable. The intricate system of arches, corridors, and underground chambers—known as the hypogeum—offers a fascinating glimpse into ancient Roman ingenuity.

Walking through the Colosseum today is like stepping back in time. The worn stone steps, towering walls, and panoramic views from the upper tiers create a powerful sense of connection to history. Informational displays and guided tours help bring the stories of gladiators, emperors, and everyday Romans to life, making the visit both educational and immersive.

The surrounding area, including the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, adds further depth to the experience, allowing visitors to explore the broader context of ancient Roman civilization. Early morning or late afternoon visits are recommended to avoid crowds and enjoy better lighting for photography.

Despite heavy tourism, the Colosseum retains an undeniable aura of majesty and resilience. It is not just a monument, but a symbol of Rome’s enduring legacy. A visit here is essential for anyone interested in history, architecture, or simply experiencing one of the world’s greatest cultural treasures.

text:
Colosseum is such an iconic historical landmark that is a must see for visitors to Rome.

To make the review useful for others, I would like you to take a look at the pictures of the different viewpoints of the interior, and the map layout of the accessible area with basic ticket.

Recommend to buy a combo ticket for the Colosseum and Roman Forum since they are next to each other, and upon exiting the Colosseum you can continue back to the center of Rome through the Roman Forum.
